description: The live wire is the gap between the people doing the work and the people holding the money. Take the professionalism seriously and never treat the community served as passive.

questions.text: How do funder priorities change what your programs actually do?
questions.lands_because: The central structural tension of the sector. Framing it as a systemic force rather than a personal compromise gets a real answer.
followups: What would you do differently with unrestricted money?

questions.text: What are you required to measure, and what actually tells you the work is working?
questions.lands_because: Outputs versus outcomes is a genuine methodological problem here, not a dodge, and practitioners have thought hard about the gap.
followups: What is the signal you trust that would never make a grant report?

questions.text: What does the community you serve ask for that funders will not pay for?
questions.lands_because: Centers the people served as agents with their own account of what they need, and exposes the mismatch without making the guest attack a funder by name.
followups: Have you ever funded it anyway?

questions.text: What happens in your organization when a grant cycle ends and the need does not?
questions.lands_because: Funding cliffs are the operational reality of the sector - staff losses, program shutdowns, relationships broken - and produce concrete stories.
followups: What does that do to the people you were serving?

questions.text: How do you talk about the work to donors versus how you talk about it in the staff meeting?
questions.lands_because: Names the two-register communication everyone in the sector performs, in a way that is understanding rather than accusatory.
followups: Does the donor version ever start to distort the work itself?

questions.text: What would it look like if your organization succeeded so completely that it should close?
questions.lands_because: The institutional self-perpetuation question, asked as an aspiration rather than an accusation. It reliably produces something thoughtful.
followups: Is anything in the structure working against that?
